summary: Resolve conversation ownership once and seek bounded identity and routing history

replay.detail: No claim replay or projection rules change; existing claims supply the same owner and route selections.

schema.detail: Adds partial accepted-time indexes for sparse conversation identity fields, actual-state source selection and runtime origins. Existing databases create the indexes on open without a schema version transition; no claims or existing indexes are removed.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; mixed-build members retain the existing replication contract.

compatibility.detail: No client-v0, peer protocol, pairing or harness contract change. Conversation routing and native reads reuse one pinned owner identity.

downtime.detail: Measurement pending on a production-size, checkpointed, disposable mode-0600 offline copy containing none of the five indexes. Run first_open_index_cost in release mode with --locked and --features test-support, passing --in-place-scratch before the copy path: it modifies that scratch in place without further database copies. It measures baseline owner reads and rolled-back claim inserts, actual combined Store::open time with sampled WAL peak, indexed owner reads/inserts and query plans, index bytes, then individual DROP/CREATE rebuild times and PASSIVE checkpoint progress. Rebuild timing benefits from freelist reuse and is not first-install per-index timing. Numbers remain to be filled after the run; Store::open is only the synchronous store-opening component of daemon unavailability, and offline checkpoint progress does not prove keep-up under live traffic. Index creation still runs before API availability; if it takes more than a few seconds, move it out of startup before rollout. Subsequent opens reuse the indexes.

manual.detail: No operator steps or identity migration required.

recovery.detail: The added indexes do not alter stored claims and older binaries ignore them. Reinstalling an older binary leaves the extra indexes in place.
